title: Casebound canonical event
description: Canonical timeline event v0.1 (PRD Section 10). The validation source of truth, mirrored by casebound/normalize/schema.py. Every factual claim in a report must resolve to one of these events by event_id.

event_id.description: Stable content hash (SHA-256 hex) of the normalized core fields. Always derived, never authored.

datetime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp normalized to UTC, with a trailing Z.

timestamp_raw.description: The original timestamp string exactly as found in the source.

source_timezone.description: The timezone used to derive datetime (an IANA name such as America/New_York, or UTC, or the literal assumed_utc when no zone was known).

timestamp_desc.description: How the timestamp relates to the event.

message.description: A short human-readable summary of the event.

host.description: Hostname or system identifier, or null when unknown.

principal.description: Account, user, or SID associated with the event, or null when unknown.

action.description: A normalized snake_case verb, for example process_create, logon, file_write.

object.description: The primary target (process path, file path, registry key, remote endpoint), or null when not applicable.

source_tool.description: The tool whose output produced the record.

source_artifact.description: The originating artifact, for example Security.evtx, $MFT, NTUSER.dat UserAssist.

details.description: A structured object holding source-specific fields.

attack_techniques.description: ATT&CK mappings, each recording its technique id and how the mapping was made.

technique_id.description: ATT&CK technique or sub-technique id, for example T1059 or T1059.001.

mapping_source.description: How the mapping was made, for example rule_tag or mapping_table.

ioc_refs.description: References into the extracted IOC set.

raw_ref.description: Pointer back to the source record for audit: the source file plus a record or line identifier.

source_file.description: The source file or export the record came from.

record.description: Line number or record id within the source file.

tags.description: Free-form labels, for example an episode id or analyst tags.
